title: Robust mixed-degradation person Re-identification via structural consistency distillation
mechanism: Targets "mixed-degradation" ReID (fog/rain/snow/brightness coexisting), framing the problem as two coupled shifts: an inter-domain centroid gap between clean and degraded features, and an intra-domain distortion of the identity topology inside the degraded domain. The Structural Consistency Distillation (SCD) module aligns a degraded-image branch to a training-only clean-image reference branch using Fused Gromov-Wasserstein (FGW) distance, which combines a Wasserstein term (cross-domain sample transport for global alignment) with a Gromov-Wasserstein term (preserving pairwise relational geometry within each domain), solved jointly under one entropy-regularized Sinkhorn optimal-transport plan with balance weight alpha. The Clean Feature Restoration (CFR) module applies EWC/Fisher-information regularization to penalize changes to parameters important for clean-image recognition, mitigating catastrophic forgetting; both modules are backbone-agnostic, feature-level, and add zero inference cost (clean branch dropped at test).
transfer_to_occluded: Treat occluded vs holistic images as the "degraded vs clean" domain pair and apply the Fused Gromov-Wasserstein alignment: use the Wasserstein term to pull occluded-sample features toward a training-only holistic reference branch (global centroid correction) while the Gromov-Wasserstein term enforces that the pairwise relational geometry among identities is preserved despite missing body regions. The key transferable trick is preserving intra-identity *relational structure* (GWD on pairwise distance matrices) rather than only matching absolute feature positions — occlusion warps the manifold topology of an ID, so distilling relational consistency from a holistic teacher could regularize occluded embeddings without needing aligned part correspondences. The EWC/CFR idea also transfers: when fine-tuning on occluded data, Fisher-weighted regularization against a holistic-trained checkpoint could prevent forgetting of discriminative cues that survive in visible regions.
novel_component: Casting domain alignment as Fused Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport that simultaneously corrects the global distribution shift (Wasserstein term) AND preserves the intra-domain pairwise relational topology of identities (Gromov-Wasserstein term) within one Sinkhorn plan — distilling *relational structure* from a clean teacher branch, not just centroid matching, with the teacher branch dropped entirely at inference.

title: A Semantic-Aware Attention and Visual Shielding Network for Cloth-Changing Person Re-Identification
mechanism: SAVS uses an SCHP human-parsing map to build two derived views of each image: a foreground image (background zeroed) and a "visual shielding/rendering image" where clothing-region pixels (upper clothes + pants) are replaced by random pixels drawn from a per-batch shuffled clothing-pixel pool. The Human Semantic Attention (HSA) module runs the foreground image through ResNet50 + an SE-style channel-attention (GAP→FC-ReLU→FC-Sigmoid) and channelwise-multiplies the resulting weights into the original Swin-T feature map to suppress background and emphasize human-semantic channels. The Visual Clothes Shielding (VCS) module (training-only) encodes the clothes-corrupted rendering image with the shared Swin-T and applies an L2 semantic-alignment loss forcing its feature to match the clean-image feature, so the network learns to ignore clothing pixels and rely on clothing-irrelevant cues (face, head, legs, feet, shape); total loss = cross-entropy + circle loss + alignment loss.
transfer_to_occluded: Adapt the VCS "corrupt-a-parsed-region + feature-consistency loss" trick to occlusion: use human parsing (or an occluder mask) to identify non-target/occluded regions, synthesize occlusion by replacing those pixels with random pixels sampled from a per-batch pool, then add an L2/MSE alignment loss pulling the corrupted-image feature toward the clean-image feature. This is a training-only, self-supervised occlusion-augmentation regularizer that teaches the backbone to produce features invariant to corrupted/missing regions, without needing extra inference modules or pose at test time. The batch-pool pixel-shuffle (rather than zero/black masking) is the transferable detail — it injects realistic distractor texture instead of constant fills, which better mimics real occluders.
novel_component: The per-batch "shielding pixel pool": clothing-region pixels are shuffled across the whole batch and each target pixel is replaced by a randomly sampled pool pixel, then a feature-consistency (MSE) loss aligns the corrupted-view feature with the clean-view feature — a self-supervised way to force invariance to a chosen semantic region without relying on holistic-only features or generative models.

title: Texture-aware transformer with pose-patch mapping for occluded person re-identification
mechanism: TTPM is a ViT + HRNet pipeline with three parts and no occlusion-sample augmentation. A Multi-patch Feature Encoder encodes intra-patch and inter-patch features (re-grouping patches at 2x scale with the cls token). Pose-Patch Mapping (PPM) builds a fine-grained, per-patch positional correspondence between M pose keypoints and N patches via a learned similarity S = gamma*D_M - eta*S_M that combines an affine-extended Mahalanobis distance and affine-extended cosine similarity, gates out low-confidence keypoints by a heatmap-confidence threshold, and selects the argmax-similarity patch per keypoint, thereby down-weighting occluded patches without coarse global pose mapping. A Texture-Aware Decoder (context-extraction MHSA layers + texture-extraction MHCA layers using pose-filtered features as queries) leverages texture distinctiveness to separate the target from non-target pedestrian occluders. An auxiliary pose loss penalizes high cosine similarity between human-part and non-human (background) features.
transfer_to_occluded: Two directly usable ideas for occluded ReID. (1) The pose loss L_p that explicitly minimizes cosine similarity between body-part features and non-human/background features — a cheap regularizer to suppress occluder/background leakage into the identity embedding, applicable to any pose- or part-based occluded model. (2) The texture-distinctiveness decoder channel aimed specifically at non-target PEDESTRIAN occlusion: when the occluder is itself a person, pose/structure cues fail (same skeleton topology), so using texture appearance distinctiveness (via pose-filtered queries cross-attending to contextual features) to push apart target vs distractor-person is a concrete mechanism for the under-addressed person-on-person occlusion case. Also transferable: replacing coarse pose-to-global mapping with a per-keypoint-to-patch confidence-gated argmax correspondence (Mahalanobis+cosine affine similarity) to localize visible regions.
novel_component: A confidence-gated per-keypoint-to-patch correspondence learned via an affine-extended Mahalanobis + cosine similarity matrix (instead of coarse pose-to-global-feature mapping), combined with a pose loss that explicitly drives down similarity between human-part and non-human features — together separating occlusion semantics from identity semantics at patch granularity, with a texture-distinctiveness channel specifically targeting person-on-person occlusion.

title: ColorSketchNet: Unifying color, sketch and texture for modality-agnostic multi-modal person re-identification
mechanism: For multi-modal ReID (query = text / sketch / text+sketch, gallery = RGB), a training-only Color Sketch Generator synthesizes an auxiliary "colored sketch" modality from RGB photos (dynamic lighting correction via EnlightenGAN+CLAHE, contour extraction via Difference-of-Gaussian into the YUV luminance channel, color injected through YUV channel replication), giving a bridge modality that holds attributes each real query modality lacks. An Attribute Compensation and Refinement Module (ACRM) then uses cross-attention between this bridge and the sketch/text features: it scores what is MISSING as (1 − attention similarity), injects only that complementary content via channel-wise gating + residual normalization, and in a second refinement stage subtracts redundant/noisy injected content weighted by photo-similarity to suppress auxiliary-modality artifacts. A unified alignment scheme (identity matching, a tri-directional structural anchor loss on the color sketch, intra-class compactness, content consistency) aligns all modalities; the auxiliary modality and ACRM are dropped at inference.
transfer_to_occluded: The dissimilarity-driven dual-stage compensation is directly portable to occlusion. Treat occluded body regions as "missing attributes" and a holistic reference (a pose prototype, a holistic-image feature, or a clean part-feature memory) as the bridge: use cross-attention to compute a (1 − similarity) "missing-ness" mask over body parts/channels, inject only the missing content via channel gating + residual term, then run a refinement stage that subtracts content already present/inconsistent with the reference (weighted by reference-similarity) to avoid filling occluded regions with hallucinated or occluder-derived features. This separates "fill what is missing" from "remove what is corrupted/distractor" in one module, and the whole bridge+compensation apparatus is training-only so it adds zero inference cost — attractive for occluded ReID feature completion that today often hallucinates or copies occluder content.
novel_component: Explicit dissimilarity-gated compensation: quantify what a modality LACKS as (1 − cross-attention similarity) to a complete bridge reference, inject only that missing content via channel gating + residual, then a refinement step that subtracts redundant/noisy injected content weighted by reference-similarity — decoupling "add missing" from "suppress noise/distractors" inside one attention module.

title: Context-Aided Semantic-Aware Self-Alignment for Video-Based Person Re-Identification
mechanism: CSSA learns pixel-level part labels without any external pose/parsing model: it separates foreground from background by the heuristic that foreground feature maps have stronger L2-norm response, clusters foreground pixels via k-means across a clip (Np=6 fixed clusters), and uses cluster IDs as pseudo-labels to iteratively train a pixel-wise part classifier producing Np+1 confidence maps (parts plus background/occlusion). A CARE module aggregates the whole clip into a denoised video-level embedding (encoder-decoder with an identity cross-entropy bottleneck) and uses its cross-pixel cosine similarity to each frame pixel as a weighted residual gate that amplifies pixels consistent with the dominant identity and suppresses clutter/occluders. SGFA then builds the global feature pair-wise: each semantic part's contribution to the aggregated global vector is weighted by the product of its query and gallery confidence scores, so a part counts only when reliable in both images.
novel_component: Pair-wise (query-AND-gallery) reliability gating: instead of fixing each image's feature independently, SGFA weights part n by the product s_n^q · s_n^g of its confidence in BOTH the probe and the candidate, so a body part influences the global descriptor only when it is jointly visible/reliable in the specific pair being compared.
transfer_to_occluded: Apply SGFA's pair-wise reliability product to occluded image ReID: when scoring a probe against each gallery candidate, weight each body part's contribution by the product of the part's visibility/confidence in the probe AND in that candidate (recomputed per pair), rather than a single self-visibility mask. This makes a region count only when it is uncorrupted on both sides — directly addressing the occluded-ReID failure where a part visible in the probe but occluded in the gallery still injects noise. The L2-norm-response foreground heuristic also offers a cheap occluder/background suppressor (occluders/background give weaker feature norm than the target body) usable to derive a soft visibility map without a parsing model.

title: Categorical Attention: Fine-grained Language-guided Noise Filtering Network for Occluded Person Re-Identification (FLaN-Net)
mechanism: FLaN-Net builds a CLIP-based pipeline that constructs an occlusion-aware fine-grained textual prompt "A photo of a [S*] person with [A*] partially occluded by [O*]," where three categorical pseudo-word tokens are learned by textual inversion from the image: S* (subject/identity description), A* (visible attributes), and O* (the occluding object). A* and O* are each produced by a separate fine-grained noise-filtering network in which a small set of learnable queries cross-attend to local patch features (so different query categories latch onto visible-attribute regions vs. occluder regions), then average-pool into a token. A cross-attention module uses the textual prompt as query and visual features as key/value (s_att) to steer the image encoder toward visible, identity-relevant regions, and a dynamic weighting fusion module combines global-visual, textual, and cross-attention features with weights derived from each feature's prediction-entropy (uncertainty), giving reliable features larger weight. Trained with contrastive + triplet + ID + ArcFace losses; inference uses only the image-encoder feature.
transfer_to_occluded: This paper IS occluded ReID, so the ideas are native rather than cross-subfield, but two components are concretely reusable in a different occluded pipeline: (1) Categorical learnable queries that explicitly separate "visible-attribute" tokens (A*) from "occluder" tokens (O*) via cross-attention to patches — i.e., learning an explicit occluder-description token forces the model to model the distractor rather than ignore it, which could be added to a non-CLIP backbone (e.g., Swin/PSG) as an auxiliary "occluder branch" whose features are pushed apart from identity features. (2) The entropy-based dynamic fusion: weight each candidate feature stream (global vs. part vs. pose-gated) by the entropy of its own ID-prediction distribution, so low-confidence (heavily occluded) streams are automatically down-weighted at the feature-fusion stage — a drop-in, training-only reliability gate that needs no extra labels and could replace fixed weights in a multi-branch occluded model.
novel_component: Per-feature entropy-as-uncertainty dynamic weighting: each fused feature stream's contribution weight is computed from the entropy of that stream's own softmax ID-classification distribution (lower entropy = more reliable = larger weight, via a softmax over Max(E)-E). This is a cheap, label-free, self-calibrating reliability gate that turns the classifier's own confidence into fusion weights and is transferable to any multi-branch ReID model where some branches degrade under occlusion.

title: Attribute Guidance With Inherent Pseudo-label For Occluded Person Re-identification (AG-ReID)
mechanism: Built on CLIP-ReID, AG-ReID mines fine-grained attributes from a frozen CLIP without extra annotations via a two-stage scheme. Stage 1 (cross-modal alignment) trains per-attribute learnable prompt tokens (CoOp-style, one set of learnable tokens per attribute category like color/hairstyle/accessories) with a SupCon loss, then uses an attribute encoder (4 self-attention layers on the image feature) to predict attribute tokens aligned to these CLIP-derived "attribute pseudo-labels." Stage 2 (dual guidance) fine-tunes the image encoder with both holistic text-prompt guidance (cross-entropy) and the fine-grained attribute pseudo-label alignment loss, plus standard ID + triplet losses. Inference uses only the ViT-B/16 image encoder, so cost matches CLIP-ReID.
transfer_to_occluded: The noise-masking attribute alignment loss: because attribute pseudo-labels encode the collective/majority attribute semantics of an identity, an occluded image's predicted attribute token at an occluded body region will mismatch the identity-level pseudo-label. AG-ReID masks out per-attribute alignment pairs whose cosine similarity falls below a threshold (set automatically per-dataset via Otsu's method to maximize inter-class variance), so the loss is computed only on reliable (visible) attribute matches and noisy occluded ones are dropped. This is a concrete, annotation-free, self-supervised way to detect-and-discard occluded/corrupted local features during training using consistency against an identity-level prototype, and the Otsu auto-thresholding removes manual per-dataset tuning — directly applicable to suppressing occluder-corrupted part features in any part/attribute-based occluded ReID model.
novel_component: Per-attribute CoOp prompts (each attribute category gets its own learnable token group) turn a frozen CLIP into a fine-grained attribute pseudo-labeler with zero manual annotation, and an Otsu-thresholded similarity noise-mask then automatically drops the attribute pairs that are inconsistent with the identity's majority semantics — a data-driven "is this local cue reliable?" gate trained only against an identity-level attribute prototype.

title: Heterogeneous Generative Tokens and Distance-Aware Recovery Network for Occluded Person Re-Identification
mechanism: A dual-stream ViT (holistic ViT-B/16 global stream + Swin-based part stream). The part stream: (1) SPG builds variable-scale "semantic patches" by windowed spatial pooling into cluster centers plus local multi-head attention, then refines them by alternating CLS-merge / patch-key-value transformer layers to inject global context; (2) AHSTG scores each semantic patch with a Discrimination Indicator Score (self-attention of CLS to patch) and Relevance Indicator Score (cosine affinity to identity), sums and softmax-normalizes them, selects the top-K as cluster centers, and generates K heterogeneous tokens of differing scale/shape via score-biased attention — tokens whose aggregated patches all have low scores are labeled as occlusion; (3) DFR projects the K selected token indices into a 2D grid, computes planar Euclidean distance between spatially adjacent heterogeneous tokens, and where the gap is large (inferred occlusion) inserts a recovery token, then recovers it by a softmax-over-negative-distance weighted aggregation of neighbor tokens so spatially closer neighbors contribute more. Trained with weighted-by-score ID loss + triplet on both streams; final descriptor concatenates global, part, and recovery features. Reports 71.8/62.3 on Occluded-Duke.
transfer_to_occluded: Distance-aware neighbor weighting for occluded-region recovery: rather than completing a missing/occluded region by uniform or pure attention-based aggregation (as in MAE-style or FCFormer completion), assign each visible neighbor token a weight = softmax(-Euclidean distance in the spatial token grid), so spatially nearer tokens dominate the reconstruction. Combine with the gap-detection trick — project surviving discriminative tokens into 2D, measure inter-token distance, and where a large spatial gap appears, infer an occlusion and insert a learnable recovery token to be filled. This is a cheap, prior-driven (spatial-locality) alternative/complement to learned attention completion and could be dropped into any token-level feature-completion module in an occluded ReID pipeline.
novel_component: The distance-aware recovery weighting: completing an occluded token by aggregating neighbors with weights = softmax(-planar Euclidean distance) in the spatial token grid, encoding the prior that spatially closer features carry more relevant information than a uniform/attention average — plus detecting occlusion as a large spatial gap between surviving discriminative tokens and inserting a recovery token there.

title: Spectrum-guided feature enhancement network for event person re-identification
mechanism: SFE-Net targets event-camera (not RGB) person ReID on a ResNet-50 backbone with two modules. (1) MSAM (Multi-grain Spectrum Attention Mechanism) denoises sparse, noisy event features by converting them to the frequency domain via FFT, applying input-adaptive Gaussian low-pass filters (predicted by GAP+FC) at three convolutional receptive-field scales to suppress high-frequency noise, then a Semantics Interaction Mechanism (self-attention) re-enriches contextual semantics; residual connections re-inject low-frequency structure. (2) CPDM (Consecutive Patch Dropout Module) splits the feature map T(x) into m=8 horizontal patches and produces m incomplete feature maps by erasing each patch in turn, training a separate ID+triplet head per incomplete map so the model is forced to find discriminative cues across all body regions; CPDM is removed at test time (only the global descriptor f_p is used for retrieval).
transfer_to_occluded: CPDM's "inverse-PCB" consecutive patch dropout is directly relevant to occluded ReID: during training, systematically zero out each horizontal body stripe one at a time and supervise an ID/triplet loss on each resulting incomplete feature map, forcing the network to extract discriminative identity cues from every region rather than collapsing onto a single dominant (often occlusion-vulnerable) region. This is a structured, region-complete simulation of occlusion that, unlike random erasing/DropBlock, guarantees each region is dropped exactly once per sample and reuses the same drop pattern across the feature stack — a cheap training-time regularizer that adds zero test-time cost (heads discarded at inference) and should improve robustness when query/gallery has missing body parts.
novel_component: The CPDM consecutive-patch-dropout idea: rather than random region erasing, deterministically generate a full set of "leave-one-stripe-out" incomplete feature maps and attach a per-incomplete-map identity head, so the model is explicitly trained to be discriminative from any single surviving region while paying nothing at test time.

title: Causal Clothes-Invariant Feature Learning for Cloth-Changing Person Re-ID (CCIL)
mechanism: Models clothing as a confounder C in a structural causal model X←C→Y and replaces likelihood training P(Y|X) with causal-intervention training P(Y|do(X))=Σ_c P(Y|X,c)·P(c) via backdoor adjustment, cutting the "clothing shortcut" backdoor path. Three modules implement it: a Confounder Dictionary storing each clothing item as a multivariate Gaussian N(μ,σ²) with prior P(c) (EMA-updated, clothing features isolated by reverse-attention masking of the identity map), an Intervention Module that samples K diverse per-clothing features, condition-injects them into the image feature and uses the NWGM trick (Eq.12) to pull the classifier out of the Σ_c sum so the whole intervention is one classification, and a Disentangle Regularization (orthogonal + KL + feature-separation losses) keeping clothing reps identity-free. Backbone-agnostic (ResNet-50 / ViT); causal/clothing streams used only in training, inference uses the identity stream alone.
transfer_to_occluded: Recast the occluder as a confounder and apply the same backdoor-adjustment recipe: build an "Occluder Dictionary" of occlusion patterns/regions stored as Gaussians with priors P(occluder), then train with P(Y|do(X))=Σ_occluder P(Y|X,occluder)·P(occluder), marginalizing over occluders so the model cannot exploit occluder-identity spurious correlations (e.g. a particular bicycle/car/pole co-occurring with certain galleries or cameras). Two concretely transferable tricks: (1) the reverse-attention masking that isolates the confounder feature from the identity feature map — directly usable to separate occluder-region features from body features without external segmentation; (2) representing each confounder as a sampled Gaussian rather than a stored feature, giving cheap synthetic occluder augmentation at the feature level. The NWGM trick keeps the marginalization a single classification, so it's nearly free at training time and zero-cost at inference.
novel_component: The NWGM-approximated backdoor adjustment implemented as a feature-level Confounder Dictionary: each nuisance factor is stored as an EMA-updated Gaussian N(μ,σ²) with a prior, K samples are drawn and condition-injected into the identity feature, and the classifier is moved outside the Σ_c sum (NWGM) so marginalizing over the confounder costs one forward pass — turning the abstract "intervene over all confounder values" into a cheap, train-only operation that disappears at inference.

title: See What You Seek: Semantic Contextual Integration for Cloth-Changing Person Re-Identification
mechanism: A CLIP-based framework (SCI) learns two dual learnable prompts, one for ID ("a photo of a [X]...[X] person") and one for clothing ("a photo of the [X]...[X] clothes"). The Semantic Separation Enhancement (SSE) module disentangles confounders at the TEXT-embedding level by orthogonal projection: it projects the clothing text feature onto the ID text feature and subtracts it (F_ort = F_id - proj(F_clo onto F_id)), removing the clothing-aligned component while preserving implicit positive ID semantics. The Semantic-Guided Interaction Module (SIM) then uses these purged text features to guide the visual encoder via a non-local operation plus cross-attention (Transformer decoder), with ablation showing non-local beats self-attention by +4.6 R-1 on cloth-changing because it aggregates from spatially distant but semantically related regions.
transfer_to_occluded: Apply the text-level orthogonal-projection disentanglement to occlusion: learn a dual prompt for the OCCLUDER/distractor (e.g. "a photo of the [X]...[X] occluder") alongside the ID prompt, then orthogonalize the occluder text feature out of the ID text feature (F_ort = F_id - proj of F_occ onto F_id) and use the purged ID text feature to guide the visual encoder via the non-local SIM. Because the non-local operation aggregates from spatially distant but semantically relevant regions, it is well suited to occluded ReID where visible body parts are scattered far from the occluded/corrupted region — letting the model pull ID evidence from non-adjacent visible patches rather than local self-attention that gets dominated by the occluder. The orthogonalization gives a clean way to subtract a known nuisance direction (occluder appearance) without an auxiliary parser.
novel_component: Disentangling a nuisance factor by vector orthogonal projection in the TEXT embedding space: project the nuisance (clothing) text feature onto the ID text direction and subtract it, purging the nuisance-aligned component of ID features without any auxiliary visual model — a cheap, parser-free disentanglement that generalizes to any named confounder (including occluders).

title: Adaptive Occlusion-Aware Network for Occluded Person Re-Identification
mechanism: AOANet uses a Swin-S backbone plus two modules. The Adaptive Position Extractor (APE) defines 4 learnable "part catchers" (query vectors) that cross-attend to high-level features f4, then self-attend + FFN, and are fused with shallow FPN features (f1,f2) via MLP+sigmoid to produce 4 soft spatial part-region maps P=[P1..P4] (head, upper body, thigh, lower leg); these maps are supervised by PifPaf pose labels during training only, so no pose model is needed at inference. Local features come from Weighted Average Pooling GAP(interp(f4)⊙P_i). At inference the Occlusion Awareness Module (OAM) computes a per-part occlusion weight as the normalized spatial area of each region map, takes the element-wise minimum of the two images' per-part weights, and forms the final similarity as a weighted sum of the 5 per-part Euclidean distances (global feature weight fixed to 1). Trained with id+triplet on global features, average triplet on parts, and a cross-entropy region loss; reaches 70.6 mAP / 81.2 R1 on Occluded-Duke.
transfer_to_occluded: Two directly transferable ideas. (1) The OAM pairwise matching rule: derive a per-part visibility/occlusion weight (here just the spatial area of the learned region mask), then for a query-gallery pair take the MIN of the two weights per part before weighting that part's distance — so a part contributes only when it is visible in BOTH images, and the global feature is always kept at weight 1 as a fallback. This is a simple, learning-free, symmetric "common-visible support" rule that can wrap any part-based occluded ReID model and is directly applicable to an occluded-ReID setup that already has part/keypoint visibility scores. (2) Pose-distillation: supervise spatial part-region extractors with pose labels at TRAIN time but drop the pose model at TEST time, so pose-estimation noise on heavily-occluded test images never propagates into the features — relevant because pose error on occluded images is a known failure mode.
novel_component: The "min-of-pairwise occlusion weights" matching rule: instead of weighting each part by a single image's visibility, weight it by the minimum of the query's and gallery's part-visibility, so a body part only influences the score when it is co-visible in both images — a symmetric pair-comparability gate that requires no extra training and keeps the always-available global feature at fixed weight 1.

title: Occluded person Re-Identification with noise injection
mechanism: Treats large-scale vehicle images (auto-collectable via license-plate recognition, framed as "positive-incentive noise") as a free training resource for occluded person ReID. Two strategies: ENI alternates the training set between person-only and vehicle-only/mixed epochs every S epochs as a regularizer; INI synthesizes realistic vehicle-occluded persons by copy-pasting a randomly-sized cropped vehicle segment into the lower-body region of person images (height-ratio r controls occlusion placement). A dual-branch CNN fuses global (avg+max pool) and local (spatial-partition + max pool) features, supervised by ID cross-entropy on both branches plus triplet loss on the global feature; no parsing nets or manual masks needed.
transfer_to_occluded: Use real out-of-domain vehicle (or generic object) crops as the occluder source for copy-paste augmentation instead of synthetic gray patches or random erasing, and inject them with a controlled height-ratio so the paste lands on the lower body to mimic real vehicle-induced occlusion. This produces texture-and-color-realistic distractor occluders that better match deployment-time occlusions than random-erasing, and the epoch-wise alternation between clean and occluder-domain data acts as a regularizer pushing the model toward occlusion-invariant features — both are drop-in, annotation-free, and backbone-agnostic for any occluded ReID pipeline.
novel_component: Reframing an "unwanted noise" domain (vehicle images) as positive-incentive noise (π-noise) that, via information-theoretic argument, reduces the recognition task's conditional entropy — and operationalizing it as a cheap, annotation-free occluder source for realistic copy-paste occlusion augmentation rather than treating it as data to discard.

title: Hierarchical fusion and local-aware transformer for occluded person re-identification
mechanism: HFLAT is a ViT-based occluded ReID model with three modules over the patch token sequence. (1) Feature Hierarchical Fusion Module (FHFM): computes each patch's relative importance to the [CLS] token as I_i = M_cls,i * ||z_i|| / sum, sorts patches by importance, splits them into 4 equal-size sub-sequences (most->least important), and cumulatively fuses them (F1=top, F2=F1+med, F3=F2+mid, F4=F3+low) so high-importance patches contribute to all fused levels — amplifying key-region identity cues. (2) Feature Separation Module (FSM): an MLP + 3x3 conv + sigmoid produces a patch-level saliency map a, splitting features into foreground (F*a) and background (F*(1-a)) with a foreground-background contrastive loss, suppressing background/occlusion without external pose/parsing. (3) Local Feature Extraction Module (LFEM): appends 4 learnable local tokens (top-to-bottom body regions) and uses local-aware masked multi-head attention where a binary Mask restricts attention so patches and their local token only attend within the same region, extracting 4 fine-grained part features. Final descriptor concatenates CLS, fused, foreground and 4 local features. Reports 64.7/79.6 (mAP/R1) on Occluded-DukeMTMC, 84.9/89.8 on Occluded-ReID.
transfer_to_occluded: Two directly usable ideas (the paper IS occluded ReID, so these are native): (1) The attention-magnitude saliency for foreground/background separation — derive a per-patch foreground probability from a lightweight conv-sigmoid head trained ONLY by a foreground-background contrastive loss (no pose/parsing labels), then suppress occluder/background tokens; this is an external-prior-free occluder gate, attractive because pose estimators fail under occlusion. (2) The importance-ranked cumulative fusion (FHFM): rank patches by CLS-attention*norm and let high-confidence (likely visible) patches contribute to every fusion level while low-importance (likely occluded) patches contribute least — a soft, label-free visibility weighting that downweights corrupted regions without a hard mask. The region-restricted masked attention with learnable part tokens is also a clean parsing-free way to get part features robust to missing regions.
novel_component: Importance-ranked CUMULATIVE hierarchical fusion (FHFM): instead of pooling all tokens equally or hard-masking occluded ones, sort patch tokens by relative importance to CLS (attention*norm), partition into ordered tiers, and fuse cumulatively (F_k = F_{k-1} + tier_k) so the most-confident/visible patches are reinforced across all fusion levels while uncertain/occluded patches enter only the last level. This is a soft, fully label-free way to weight tokens by reliability — transferable as an uncertainty-aware token aggregation that avoids both equal pooling and brittle hard occlusion masks.

title: Cloth-debiasing with Stable Diffusion in Cloth-changing Person Re-identification
mechanism: Uses a Stable Diffusion virtual-try-on pipeline (LaDi-VTON) to generate cloth-changed copies of each pedestrian with a unified, consistent clothing color/type, so the model can no longer rely on clothing as an ID cue. Generation is controlled by SCHP body-segmentation masks (clothing regions are inpainted while non-clothing body parts are kept fixed) and OpenPose keypoints (to keep the synthesized image faithful to body geometry/pose); two threshold filters (a ReID-feature similarity filter and a batch-wise FID filter) plus manual inspection discard low-quality generations. The filtered augmented set trains a CAL baseline augmented with a centroid loss that tightens intra-ID clusters and pushes apart the centroids of same-vs-different-ID groups, yielding +6 Rank-1 / +4.4 mAP on PRCC cloth-changing.
novel_component: Pose-keypoint-conditioned, segmentation-mask-guided diffusion inpainting that edits only a targeted region (clothing) while freezing the rest of the body, paired with automatic quality gating (ReID-similarity + FID filters) so only geometrically/identity-faithful synthetic samples are admitted to training.
transfer_to_occluded: Repurpose the mask-guided, pose-conditioned diffusion inpainting from "swap the clothing region" to "fill the occluded region": use a body-segmentation/visibility mask to mark missing or occluder-corrupted body parts, then inpaint them with OpenPose-keypoint-conditioned Stable Diffusion to synthesize plausible body content, generating occlusion-augmented training pairs (or recovered query images). Critically, transfer their two-stage quality gate — admit a recovered region only if its ReID-feature similarity to the clean identity is high and its FID is low — so hallucinated content is filtered before it pollutes training, addressing the chronic risk that completion/inpainting injects identity-inconsistent features in occluded ReID.

title: Beyond geometry: The power of texture in interpretable 3D person ReID
mechanism: FusionTexReIDNet is a dual-stream 3D ReID framework. Stream 1 (UVTextureNet) reconstructs a 3D human model from 2D images (RSC-Net + Texformer) and extracts appearance features from high-resolution, viewpoint-normalized UVTexture maps in a canonical UV coordinate space, so a given body region maps to a fixed UV location regardless of pose/camera; Stream 2 (3DReIDNet) processes the rendered XYZ+RGB point cloud with Dynamic Graph Convolution and an Omni-scale module. The two streams' distance matrices are fused by weighted sum and refined with KNN, attribute, and an "explainable" re-ranking that uses an Intersection-Alignment Score (IAS) over UVTexture activation maps.
transfer_to_occluded: The Intersection-Alignment Score (IAS) explainable re-ranking is directly occlusion-relevant: compute IoU between the model's activation/attention map and a visible-region (non-occluded) mask, plus a cosine alignment between query and gallery activation maps, then refine the distance matrix — multiply distance by alpha<1 when attention focuses on visible regions AND query/gallery attentions agree, and by beta>1 when attention falls on occluded/missing regions. In occluded ReID this is a self-supervised matching-side trust mechanism: down-weight matches whose discriminative evidence sits on occluder/missing pixels and reward query-gallery pairs whose visible-region attention co-aligns, without needing identity-level supervision. The canonical-UV idea (mapping body regions to fixed coordinates so the same part always aligns) is also a clean way to make two partially-occluded crops compare only on their commonly-visible parts.
novel_component: Intersection-Alignment Score (IAS): turning an explainability signal into a re-ranking operator — measure how much the model's attention overlaps the visible-body mask (IoU) and how mutually consistent query/gallery attention maps are, then asymmetrically shrink or inflate pairwise distances. It makes "is the model looking at occluded regions?" a concrete, label-free matching correction rather than a post-hoc visualization.

title: Shape-centered Representation Learning for Visible-Infrared Person Re-identification
mechanism: A dual-stream framework (appearance stream Ea + shape stream Es) for VI-ReID built on AGW. Body shape is parsed by a pre-trained SCHP human-parsing model; infrared shapes are unreliable because skin/background look similar in IR, so the parser misses limbs. Three components fix and exploit this: (1) Infrared Shape Restoration (ISR) — a spatial cross-attention at an intermediate backbone block where the query is built by summing the IR shape feature map and the IR appearance feature map, and key/value come from IR appearance features, so missing shape regions are searched for and restored from appearance; clean VIS shape features (no restoration) are mixed into the same loss batch to implicitly supervise the restoration. (2) Shape Feature Propagation (SFP) — a replicated 4th block of the appearance encoder (Es-tilde) is distilled from the shape stream at both instance level (L2) and prototype level (CE to class prototypes), so at inference the heavy shape stream and parser are dropped. (3) Appearance Feature Enhancement (AFE) — a cascaded two-stage cross-attention that uses shape features as query over appearance key/value to first pull out directly-shape-correlated appearance, then re-query to gather indirectly-related appearance, suppressing background/modality noise. Inference concatenates the distilled shape feature with the AFE-enhanced appearance feature.
transfer_to_occluded: Reframe occlusion as a "corrupted-region restoration at the feature level" problem and reuse ISR: for an occluded ID, treat the occluded/missing body regions like the missing IR limbs. Build a query by summing a body-structure feature map (e.g., pose/parsing heatmap features — exactly this repo's PSG pose branch) with the appearance feature map, and run spatial cross-attention with key/value from the appearance features, so the network searches the unoccluded regions to restore plausible features for the missing region — instead of zeroing/masking occluded parts. Critically, the supervision trick transfers cleanly: mix clean (holistic, non-occluded) samples' shape/part features into the same loss batch as the restored occluded features under a shared classifier + WRT triplet, so the holistic samples implicitly supervise restoration WITHOUT needing per-pixel ground truth for the occluded region. This is a label-free way to train feature-level completion, which prior occluded-ReID completion attempts in this repo found hard to supervise.
novel_component: The implicit, label-free supervision of feature-level restoration: clean-modality (VIS) shape features that need NO restoration are mixed into the same mini-batch and identity/triplet loss as the restored (IR) features, so the restoration module is trained purely by the shared ID classifier pulling restored and clean features of the same identity together — no per-region reconstruction target is ever specified. Pairing this with a query formed by summing the structure-map and appearance-map (so spatial misalignment/anomaly itself flags where restoration is needed) is a transferable recipe for any "one channel is corrupted/missing, a parallel clean channel exists" setting.

title: 3D-Aided Pedestrian Representation Learning for Video-Based Person Re-Identification
mechanism: Per frame, an off-the-shelf 3D human reconstruction (HMR/SMPL) produces a pedestrian mesh, which is converted to a point cloud and back-projected with image RGB; a detection-free PointPillar backbone encodes it into a pseudo-image ("pillar-based feature") whose dimensions are aligned with 2D ResNet image features. A Cross-Modal Fusion (CMF) module uses deformable cross-attention where pillar features are queries and 2D-to-3D mapping gives reference points, so sampling locations on the image are anchored at projected pedestrian body positions. A separate Shape-aware Spatial-Temporal Interaction (SSTI) module runs parallel spatial/temporal self-attention over SMPL shape parameters (β) to form a video-level 3D-shape descriptor; CMF fusion features (after temporal aggregation) and the SSTI shape feature are concatenated as the final representation, trained with cross-entropy + triplet.
transfer_to_occluded: Use an off-the-shelf 3D body reconstruction (SMPL/HMR) of the pedestrian to generate geometric reference points, then drive deformable cross-attention so the image-feature sampling locations are anchored at projected body-keypoint/mesh positions. For occluded ReID this gives a body-structure prior independent of pixel evidence: even when a region is occluded, the reconstructed mesh still provides a body-anchored query, steering attention onto plausible person regions and away from distractor occluders, and the pose/shape-derived reference points act as a soft visibility/structure guide. The SSTI idea of an appearance-independent shape descriptor (from β only) is also a complementary, occlusion-robust feature since estimated body shape is less corrupted by occluders than RGB texture.
novel_component: Deformable cross-attention where the reference points are not learned but supplied by a 2D-to-3D mapping from an off-the-shelf body reconstruction (φ: mesh point -> image location), so attention sampling is grounded on projected body geometry. The 3D mesh thus acts as a structural anchor that exists even where 2D pixels are unreliable.

title: Latent Diffusion-Guided Feature Inpainting for Occluded Person Re-Identification With Hybrid Re-Ranking
mechanism: Occlusion is reframed as a structured, invertible distortion in feature space rather than something the backbone must learn to tolerate: clean ViT features F are corrupted into occluded features F_o by an unknown transform T, and a Latent Diffusion-guided De-Occluder (DDO) learns T^-1. DDO projects occluded ViT features (768x14x14) into a 256-channel latent, runs a conditional reverse-diffusion denoiser supervised by paired clean features (a reconstruction loss L_recon = lambda*MSE + (1-lambda)*(1-cos) added to the standard denoising loss acts like classifier guidance), and decodes a reconstructed clean embedding F_clean. F_clean and F_o are then fused via multi-head cross-attention (Q from F_clean, K/V from F_o), part-pooled with a Global-Enhanced Local Token (GELT) fusion, and trained with a modified centroid triplet loss plus per-part cross-entropy. A separate Hybrid Re-Ranking (HRR) stage exploits the closed-set assumption: it computes per-identity gallery centroids, keeps only the Top-N centroids closest to the query, and runs k-reciprocal Jaccard re-ranking restricted to that centroid-pruned candidate subset.
transfer_to_occluded: This paper IS occluded ReID, so the whole pipeline is on-domain, but the single most transferable trick is treating occlusion as an explicitly invertible map T in FEATURE space and learning T^-1 with paired clean/occluded-feature supervision — instead of masking/suppressing occluded regions, you generatively reconstruct the clean identity embedding before it reaches the ReID head. Concretely transferable pieces: (1) train a feature-space de-occluder on synthetic occlusion pairs (silhouette-guided background patching + Fourier-domain adaptation to bridge synth-to-real) where the FROZEN ViT clean feature is the ground truth, so no occlusion masks are needed at test time; (2) keep both reconstructed and raw occluded features and fuse them with cross-attention (Q=clean, K/V=occluded) rather than discarding the occluded one — the reconstruction acts as a query that re-attends the raw features toward visible identity regions, which is robust when reconstruction is imperfect; (3) the reconstruction-loss-as-classifier-guidance idea turns an unconditional generative module into an identity-preserving deterministic operator, directly useful for any completion-based occluded-ReID module to avoid hallucinating wrong identities.
novel_component: Formulating occlusion as a deterministic, invertible transform T in deep-feature space and learning its inverse T^-1 via a latent diffusion model supervised by paired clean ViT features — i.e. feature-space inpainting where a reconstruction loss plays the role of classifier guidance, yielding a deterministic identity-preserving de-occluder rather than a stochastic sampler, and crucially requiring no masks/pose/parsing at inference.

title: Pose-Skeleton Guided Cross-Attention Representation Fusion for Occluded Pedestrian Re-Identification
mechanism: A ResNet-50/ViT backbone is augmented with three pose-driven modules. VARA inserts pose-keypoint-heatmap-guided soft-fusion attention into intermediate backbone layers (Conv.B2/B3) using a foreground-aware channel-attention sub-module plus a spatial cross-attention sub-module, suppressing occlusion-information diffusion before it spreads through the growing receptive field. SAM (Skeletal Area Modeling) generates soft masks for 14 predefined inter-keypoint skeletal regions via a closed-form 2D Gaussian "radiation" along each bone segment AB (Eqs. 3-5), whose intensity I(δ_A, δ_B) is modulated by the confidence scores δ of the two endpoint keypoints — so low-confidence (likely occluded) joints yield weak masks. SMCF then fuses these skeletal local features with backbone features via a Transformer cross-attention (skeletal features as query, backbone map as key/value), with the SAM weight map element-wise constraining the cross-attention map.
transfer_to_occluded: SAM's confidence-modulated skeletal-region masks are directly an occluded-ReID mechanism and transferable as a drop-in replacement for keypoint-heatmap masks. Two concrete ideas: (1) build soft masks over the inter-keypoint BONE regions (Gaussian radiation along segment AB, narrow/elongated, tunable transverse compression) instead of only at keypoints, covering the appearance area BETWEEN joints that keypoint heatmaps miss — this fills the coverage gap and reduces incomplete-region feature extraction; (2) modulate each region mask's strength by the geometric-mean/sum of its two endpoint keypoint CONFIDENCES (δ_A, δ_B) with a confidence threshold T=0.7, so occluded body parts automatically get near-zero mask response and are softly excluded, giving a continuous visibility signal grounded in pose-estimator uncertainty rather than a hard binary part-visibility flag.
novel_component: Closed-form "Skeletal Area Modeling": a per-bone 2D Gaussian mask radiated along each keypoint-pair segment, whose amplitude is gated by the product/level of the two endpoint keypoint confidences (with a threshold T). This turns pose-estimator confidence into a smooth, region-level (not point-level) visibility prior over body parts — no trainable params, robust to low-res images where pixel-level parsing masks fail.

title: Occlusion-aware Cross-modality Completion Network for Occluded Visible-Infrared Person Re-Identification
mechanism: OCCNet treats occlusion as a completion problem rather than discarding occluded regions. A shared ResNet50 extracts modality-specific token maps, then a Graph-guided Feature Completion Transformer (GFCT) builds a dynamic semantic adjacency matrix from latent token similarities and uses it as an Adaptive Graph-guided Attention bias to restrict self-attention to semantically related token pairs, completing occluded tokens by aggregating from clean contextual tokens across the whole image. A Semantic-aware Region Completion Module (SRCM) clusters tokens into semantic regions (top-K similarity prototypes), refines them with multi-order graph convolutions (Graph Context Perception), and uses Cross-modality Soft Querying to pull complementary cues from the other modality's region memory bank; a Multi-Distribution Consistency Alignment (MCA) loss aligns token-level and region-level completions to their averaged pseudo-holistic reference via symmetric KL divergence.
transfer_to_occluded: The Adaptive Graph-guided Attention idea transfers directly to single-modality occluded ReID: instead of relying on positional embeddings or fixed body-part labels, build a dynamic semantic adjacency matrix from latent token similarities computed over ALL tokens (the paper argues the global similarity graph stays reliable even when a few tokens are corrupted, since structure is set by overall contextual coherence), then use it as an attention bias so occluded tokens are repaired by aggregating from multiple semantically-related visible tokens across the image rather than from their own unreliable local responses. The pseudo-holistic-reference MCA trick — averaging two completion paths and forcing each to match the mean via symmetric KL (rather than direct mutual alignment) — is also a transferable, low-cost regularizer for stabilizing any multi-branch completion/reconstruction head in occluded ReID.
novel_component: Using a dynamically-constructed latent semantic similarity graph (over all tokens, including occluded ones) as an explicit attention-bias to drive token completion — repairing occluded regions by graph-guided aggregation from semantically related clean tokens, instead of positional encoding, parsing labels, or local neighbors. Paired with a symmetric pseudo-holistic-mean consistency loss that avoids letting one noisy completion branch bias another.

title: CFPER: Coarse-to-Fine Part-Experts Retrieval for Efficient Person Re-identification
mechanism: A ViT extracts a global feature G and N patch embeddings. A two-stage Coarse-to-Fine Dynamic Retrieval (CFDR) routes "easy" queries through an early-exit using only G, while "hard" queries proceed to a fine stage. The fine stage uses a Part-aware Mixture of Experts (PMoE): a Patch-to-Part Router (PPR), supervised by human-topology coarse body-part labels plus a Push Loss, soft-routes patches to M body-part experts (cross-attention modules) via Probability-Weighted Average Pooling, and binary visibility routing weights activate only body-relevant experts (deactivating occluded parts) to cut computation.
novel_component: A label-free, near-zero-cost occlusion/visibility detector: sort the cosine similarities between the global feature G and each patch embedding in descending order, take their first-order differences, and pick the index of the maximum difference as the split point between body patches (high similarity to global identity) and background/occlusion patches (low similarity). This treats body vs occlusion as separable classes in feature space and detects the transition without pose estimation or human parsing.
transfer_to_occluded: The first-order-difference split point on sorted G-to-patch cosine similarities is a cheap, supervision-free occlusion detector that could be dropped into an occluded-ReID pipeline to estimate which patches/parts are occluded, then drive part-visibility gating (mask occluded part tokens before matching) and a per-part visibility score for MaxSim-style partial matching — all without an external pose/parsing model. Complementary: the Push Loss that contrastively separates a learned background/occlusion feature from the foreground feature could regularize an occluder-aware feature space.

title: Structured Distilled 3D Gait Fields for Clothes-Changing Person Re-Identification in Videos
mechanism: For video clothes-changing ReID, instead of using sparse 3D skeletons or low-dimensional SMPL parameters for gait, the method distills dense 3D mesh-surface knowledge into the 2D image domain. It pre-trains per-vertex embeddings on the canonical SMPL mesh via a GCN, supervised so that embedding L2 distances match mesh geodesic distances and embedding angles match surface tangent angles; a lightweight U-Net extractor is then trained to assign every foreground pixel an embedding equal to its underlying 3D vertex's embedding, forming a per-frame "structured distilled 3D gait field" that is spatially/temporally aligned with the video. Local similarity learning plus a dual-granularity token cross-attention module (MRIE) then fuse this gait field with clothing-desensitized appearance features.
transfer_to_occluded: Adopt the dense pixel-to-3D-vertex correspondence embedding as an occlusion-aware matching substrate: train a per-pixel head that maps each foreground pixel to a canonical SMPL-vertex embedding (supervised by geodesic/tangent-consistent vertex codes). Then (a) occluded/missing body regions are explicitly detected as 3D vertices with no supporting pixel, yielding a per-vertex visibility/support map for free, and (b) two images are matched only over their shared visible 3D vertices ("common visible support"), making the comparison occlusion-robust without relying on holistic features. The cross-frame "same-vertex => consistent embedding" constraint also provides a structural prior to inpaint or down-weight corrupted regions.
novel_component: Distilling a canonical 3D-mesh's geodesic/tangent-structured per-vertex embeddings into a dense per-pixel 2D field via 3D-to-2D projection, turning sparse 3D structure into spatially-aligned dense pixel embeddings that establish explicit pixel-to-3D-vertex correspondence.
